text:
AKIEN, 2026-08-05 EVENING, VERBATIM AND IN ORDER — the correction, then the anatomy:

'um, i was just reading the 3 section b stackable learning blocks. i have no idea where that came from, but that's garbage'

'a stackable learning block may start with a door, tho i didn't call it that. it has a domain, a knowledge base. it has feedback loops. it has core questions. it does not have findings or verdicts or anything a human comments on'

'you've conflated inspectors and learning blocks.'

'an inspector is a kind of learning block a subclass'

'ok, a stackable learning block has also been called a question nexus. it has an input, which can be anything tho for now many pass or recieve json chunks. it has feedback loops coming in from probes. it has new candidate constraining questions suggested by feedback and LLM processing, probably in the evenings. it has a domain knowledge base. it has constraining questions. inside of that are two loops. i don't remember what they're for, but they're distinct. i think one controls input and one output but i'll have to find it. and then it has an output. that's a learning block. they predict and respond to the feedback on those predictions. they do learning and fail over to llm for more nodes as needed. i realized at one point such a tool could be used to gather data until it could prove almost anything. or fail in the trying. so that's a learning block. our pre build steps are each a learning block of this form. end of chunk. inspectors are also learning blocks because everything's a learning block. but inspectors jobs are defined enough that they have THEIR OWN CLASS. They have the same structure. but their KB has a list of things they are to measure and produce findings on. they fail over in the face of ambiguity using the same query-to-inference-proxy methods as everything else.'

=== THE ANATOMY, AS RULED ===

A STACKABLE LEARNING BLOCK IS A QUESTION NEXUS. The two names are one thing.

  INPUT — anything; today many pass or receive JSON chunks.
  FEEDBACK LOOPS IN, FROM PROBES.
  NEW CANDIDATE CONSTRAINING QUESTIONS — suggested by that feedback and by LLM processing, 'probably in the evenings'.
  A DOMAIN KNOWLEDGE BASE.
  CONSTRAINING QUESTIONS.
  TWO LOOPS INSIDE, DISTINCT.
  OUTPUT.

And its behaviour: it PREDICTS and RESPONDS TO THE FEEDBACK ON THOSE PREDICTIONS; it LEARNS; and it FAILS OVER TO THE LLM FOR MORE NODES AS NEEDED. His realisation, kept in his words because it is the thesis in one line: 'such a tool could be used to gather data until it could prove almost anything. or fail in the trying.'

SCOPE, STATED: 'our pre build steps are each a learning block of this form.'

WHAT IT DOES NOT HAVE: findings, verdicts, or anything a human comments on.

=== THE TWO LOOPS ARE ALREADY NAMED, IN BUILT CODE ===

He said he did not remember what they were for, guessed one controls input and one output, and would have to find it. THEY ARE IN cairn/machines/learning_block/engine.py, LINE 12: 'input -> candidates loop -> evaluation loop -> decide or escalate -> output'. So: the CANDIDATES loop generates, the EVALUATION loop kills against the constraints and leaves survivors. His guess was right in shape — candidates is the input side, evaluation the output side. Built and PROVED 2026-08-02 under ticket engine-runs-one-block, with the state log answering five questions including 'what constraint killed each loser'.

WHICH MEANS THE ENGINE IS RIGHT AND THE ORGANS BOLTED AROUND IT WERE WRONG. The inner loop conforms to the anatomy above. What does not conform is everything hung on its exit.

=== THE CONFLATION, NAMED ===

CC hung the INSPECTOR's organs on the LEARNING BLOCK, its parent. FINDING, VERDICT and DIAL are not organs of a block.

  FINDING is the INSPECTOR's OUTPUT — a specialisation of the output slot, not an extra organ. Akien: 'their KB has a list of things they are to measure and produce findings on.' The findings come out of the output because the KB says what to measure. Nothing new is added to the shape.
  VERDICT and DIAL are the HUMAN GATE ON AN INSPECTOR and the delegation machinery around it. They are a separate matter entirely, and they never belonged to the block anatomy.

WHY THE MERGE HAPPENED, AND IT IS INSTRUCTIVE: Akien's own 2026-08-01 line says of the inspector 'it too will learn as it goes' — so an inspector IS a learning block, and CC read the IS-A backwards, promoting the subclass's parts into the parent. Subtype, not identity. AN INSPECTOR IS A LEARNING BLOCK WHOSE KB IS A LIST OF THINGS TO MEASURE; A LEARNING BLOCK IS NOT AN INSPECTOR.

And inspectors get THEIR OWN CLASS — his words — 'because inspectors jobs are defined enough'. Same structure, different KB. They fail over on ambiguity by the same query-to-inference-proxy path as everything else, which is the same failover the block has, not a special one.

=== THE RECEIPT: THE SEAM CAUGHT IT ===

notes/held-learning-blocks-everywhere.json carries a literal key: 'SEAM — below here is CC's read, not Akien's words'. The five-organ anatomy (the_settled_stage_anatomy) sits BELOW that seam. Above it, his verbatim says only two things about a learning block: it can 'send a task or whatever back if the inputs are not sufficient AT ALL STEPS' (the door) and 'learning blocks logic gets pushed to graph trees or code as we go' (migration). DOOR AND MIGRATION. Nothing else. The organ list was CC's read all along and was correctly labelled as such — the discipline worked; nobody read the label.

=== TWO CONNECTIONS THIS MAKES THAT WERE NOT DRAWN BEFORE ===

(1) 'FEEDBACK LOOPS COMING IN FROM PROBES' wires the questions store's LANE ONE directly into every block. A probe's YIELD is not a statistic kept beside the system — it is a block's input. That gives the probe corpus the consumer it has been chartered without since 2026-07-22.

(2) 'NEW CANDIDATE CONSTRAINING QUESTIONS SUGGESTED BY FEEDBACK AND LLM PROCESSING, PROBABLY IN THE EVENINGS' IS THE OVERNIGHT DRAIN. notes/overnight-drain.json and the questions charter's no_drain_yet IOU ('a corpus with an intake and no drain is worse than no corpus') have been waiting for a job description. This is it: the evening pass is what turns accumulated feedback into the next round of constraining questions. The drain is not housekeeping, it is the block's learning step.

(3) 'FAIL OVER TO LLM FOR MORE NODES AS NEEDED' IS THE LIBRARIAN'S CORE LOOP, verbatim in mechanism: walk, miss, ask the resolver for NODES not answers, deposit, resubmit. §2.2 of the graph-tree brief. So the block's failover and the memory's backfill are one mechanism, not two — which is why 'everything's a learning block' is a structural claim and not a slogan.

=== WHAT IS NOW WRONG ON DISK ===

  cairn/machines/learning_block/intention+why.json — charters five organs including FINDING and VERDICT as the block's own. BUILT AND PROVED 2026-08-01, 31 teeth. The engine inside it is right; the organ list is not.
  cairn/machines/skill_block/ — built on that shape.
  tickets/skills-migrate-one-blow.json — URGENT: it migrates ALL NINE skills to 'the settled anatomy... a stratum-tagged bullet-list finding at exit'. That is the chimera, nine times, and the ticket is live. DO NOT MIGRATE UNTIL THE ANATOMY IS CORRECTED — the same reason the skills migration was already held behind the clearance ruling tonight: do not migrate onto a model just found wrong.
  tickets/learning-block-engine-track.json — the engine track is UNAFFECTED and correct.
  tickets/chart.json — its nexus definition ('input + feedback + candidate core questions + domain-specific knowledge + core questions + output, WORKED by a mini agentic loop') is the CLOSEST EXISTING STATEMENT of the true anatomy and should be read as the same object under its other name. One wording change: he says CONSTRAINING questions, not core questions.
  cairn/press_office/GraphTreeMemoryTechnicalBrief.md §3 — 'Section B: Stackable Learning Blocks' is this error written out at length. His verdict, unappealed: 'that's garbage.' §3.1's five-organ table is wrong at the root. §3.2-§3.5 are ABOUT THE HUMAN GATE, which is a real thing he said and not a learning block's anatomy — so they are misfiled rather than false, and where they land is his call. NOT REWRITTEN BY CC: the brief is his document, he is mid-edit-pass on it, and the section needs his decision about scope before prose.

=== STATUS ===

NOT CAST, NOT RULED AT THE DOOR. This is the verbatim chunk plus the immediate consequences, written down before a context restart so nothing rides in attention — which is the same discipline the learning block exists to enforce ('the reasoning a session used to hold in attention lands in a record any model can read back'). The ruling packet, the charter correction and the §3 disposition are the next acts and are Akien's to direct.
